A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Collapsed Language Models Promote Fairness and contain 19 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of the equations, figures, tables and appendix content.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-collapse measurements, regularized fine-tuning experiments and ablations in Sections 3–5, with further empirical results in Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original measurements and experiments, including the proposed regularizer's results and appendix analyses. Results attributed to previous work are distinguishable from the paper's own experiments.

M1.justification: The (U)NC3 auxiliary regularizer in Equation 3 and its combination with existing training objectives in Equation 6 are identical. No algorithm, architecture or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Training corpora and evaluation coverage are unchanged, including StereoSet, BEC-Pro, WinoBias, Bias-in-Bios, GLUE and appendix Bias-NLI experiments. The additional-model datasets and gender, neutral and random vocabulary scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding table, including MABEL, ASE, BEC, Sent-Debias, Context-Debias, FairFil and ADEPT, the StereoSet BERT+Dropout/CDA baselines, and the appendix RoBERTa/FairBERTa comparisons.

E3.justification: Training settings in Section 4.1.1, the three-epoch MLM experiment in Section 5, evaluation metrics, sample counts and appendix regularization settings are unchanged. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The standalone regularization experiment and t-SNE analysis in Section 5, regularization-strength sweep in Appendix B, and vocabulary analyses in Section 3 and Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The standard deviation used within (U)NC3 remains a method component, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–16 and the Figure 2 visualization are unchanged. For example, MABEL+(U)NC3 retains StereoSet SS 55.38 and ICAT 74.55 in Table 4; the caption correction changes no results.

T1.justification: The NC definitions, calibrated metrics, Equations 1–7 and stated conditions for neural collapse in Section 3.2.1 are identical. No mathematical reasoning, assumptions or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same claims linking debiasing with neural collapse and proposing broadly applicable regularization that improves fairness while preserving language-task performance.

C2.justification: Explanations of differing NC-metric behavior and gender-sensitive vocabulary effects remain unchanged, as do interpretations of GLUE and visualization results. Appendix D retains the same qualification about limited gains on Bias-NLI.

D1.justification: Section 4.1.1's hyperparameters and class-mean accumulation details, appendix word lists and regularization settings, and the code-access link are identical. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 74 references are unchanged. Table 4 replaces '(author?) [26]' with 'He et al. [26]', retaining the same already-cited MABEL paper; this repairs citation rendering without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The recurring header changes from 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' to 'Preprint', the first-page arXiv version/date stamp updates, and Table 4's author citation is repaired. The narrative and section/appendix organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4's caption reflows after the citation correction, and the headers and first-page arXiv stamp change visually. Figures 1–2, table structures and placements, and the remaining page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The only body edit repairs Table 4's author display, whose numbered citation already identified the same source in v1. This modest presentation correction and the header/stamp updates leave the paper's scientific content, evidence, reproducibility and organization unchanged, producing no meaningful overall quality difference.
